title: Bored!
gr: other uses of -ing and the infinitive: after adjectives, prepositions, and as a subject

can.en: I can use an -ing form or an infinitive in the places where the verb itself does not decide.

voc: tired and impatient because nothing is happening
no longer willing to put up with
relax after a period of work or tension

doing the same thing again and again

acts.title: Seven kinds of boredom, roughly
text: Ironing is, for a great many people, the most ___ job in the house.
A lecture read off the slides costs most of us our ___ after about half an hour.
After that the mind ___ , and yawning starts.
On the last hour of a long flight almost everybody is ___ to get off.
The worst boredom at work, though, is not being ___ enough — a task finished in five minutes and nothing after it.
What that produces is not tiredness. It is being ___ with having nothing to do, which is a different feeling entirely.

items.q: I was bored to ___ watching that film.
“Apathetic boredom” means you are ___ of finding enjoyment in life.
“Indifferent boredom” is a pleasant feeling that lets you ___ out after a long day.
After a long-haul flight I am usually ___ to get off the plane.
Have you experienced the ___ to fall asleep during a dull lecture?
Boredom can be a very useful ___.
If your mind ___, it means you have stopped paying attention.
Boredom means feeling ___ in a situation you want to escape from.

tts: Speaker one: Listening to my boss. She always gives you far too much information — goes into too much detail about things you do not need to know — and I am thinking, for goodness sake, just get to the point.

Speaker two: Watching a slow-moving film at the cinema. So many films are three hours long. That is a long time to be sitting in one place. I hate that feeling when you cannot sit still and you just want to stretch your legs.
Speaker three: Doing the ironing is the most boring and repetitive of all household jobs. It seems to take for ever.
Speaker four: For me it is long-haul flights. I can usually amuse myself with films and music for the first few hours, but towards the end I am absolutely desperate to get off that plane.
Speaker five: Rainy days are the worst. I get really fed up with being stuck indoors. I feel a real need to get out and do something active.

items.q: What are the speakers describing?
o: The situations that bore them most

items.q: What bores the first speaker?
o: A boss who gives far too much detail

items.q: What does the fifth speaker say about rainy days?
o: She gets fed up with being stuck indoors

tts: Speaker six: There is nothing more likely to send me to sleep than a dull lecture. The ones I hate most involve a PowerPoint presentation where the lecturer reads what is on the slides and does not give us an opportunity to discuss or ask questions. I find myself losing concentration after about half an hour, my mind starts to wander, I start yawning, and I find it really hard not to fall asleep.

Speaker seven: For me the most boring thing in the world is not having enough to keep me occupied at work. You ask your boss and they give you a simple task that you finish in five minutes, and then you are back to doing nothing. You do not want to be annoying, asking for tasks every five minutes, so you just sit there feeling awkward.

items.s: Speaker six objects to lecturers reading off their slides.
He loses concentration after about half an hour.
He finds it easy to stay awake.
Speaker seven is bored by having too much work.
Speaker seven does not want to keep asking for tasks.

tts: That is a long time to be sitting in one place.
I get really fed up with being stuck indoors.
I find it really hard not to fall asleep.
Doing the ironing is the most boring job in the house.
The most boring thing is not having enough to keep me occupied.
I am absolutely desperate to get off that plane.

items.q: “fed up with being stuck indoors” — why the -ing form?
“I find it hard not to fall asleep.” Where does the negative go?
“Doing the ironing is the most boring job.” What job is the -ing form doing?
o: It is the subject of the sentence

items.q: “desperate to get off” — what follows an adjective like desperate?

acts.title: When the verb is not the one deciding
rule: Lesson 33 dealt with verbs that choose for you. This lesson deals with everything else — the positions where the choice is made by an adjective, a preposition, or the job the phrase is doing in the sentence.
points: Always -ing. Never an infinitive. fed up with waiting, good at explaining, instead of leaving.
Usually to + infinitive: desperate to leave, difficult to explain, hard to believe.
Use -ing: Doing the ironing is boring. An infinitive subject is possible but sounds formal.
too + adjective + to; adjective + enough + to. Too tired to concentrate; old enough to know.
Put not in front of the to: I find it hard not to fall asleep.
find it hard to…, make it difficult to… The real subject moves to the end.
eg: I’m fed up with being stuck indoors.
Preposition + -ing.
She’s good at explaining things.
Preposition + -ing.
Instead of leaving, he sat down.
Preposition + -ing.
I’m desperate to get off this plane.
Adjective + to.
It’s difficult to concentrate in here.
Adjective + to, with placeholder it.
Doing the ironing is the most boring job.
-ing as subject.
I find it really hard not to fall asleep.
Negative in front of to.
The film was too long to sit through.
too + adjective + to.
He isn’t old enough to remember it.
adjective + enough + to.
That’s a long time to be sitting in one place.
to be + -ing, for an ongoing state.
acts.careful: “I look forward to hear from you” and “fed up with wait” are both wrong. After to as a preposition — look forward to, be used to, object to — the next word takes -ing.

lines: I get really fed up with [being|be|to be] stuck indoors all weekend.
She is very good at [explaining|explain|to explain] things clearly.
Towards the end I am desperate [to get|getting|get] off the plane.
[Doing|To doing|Do] the ironing is the most repetitive job there is.
I find it really hard [not to fall|to not fall|not falling] asleep, and the film was too long [to sit|for sitting|sitting] through.

items.from: I have had enough of being indoors.

steps.cue: Rewrite it with FED UP WITH
steps.a: I’m fed up with being indoors
alt: I am fed up with being indoors
steps.why: with is a preposition, so the verb takes -ing.

steps.cue: Now say you want very much to go out, with DESPERATE
alt: I am desperate to go out

items.from: The ironing is very boring. It is a job.

steps.cue: Make the activity the SUBJECT, with -ING
Now say it is hard to stay interested, with FIND IT HARD TO
steps.a: I find it hard to stay interested

items.from: The film lasted three hours. I could not sit through it.

steps.a: The film was too long to sit through

steps.cue: Now rewrite it the other way, with ENOUGH: he is not old enough to remember it
steps.a: He isn’t old enough to remember it
alt: He is not old enough to remember it

items.from: I keep falling asleep in that lecture, and I am trying not to.

steps.cue: Say it with FIND IT HARD and a NEGATIVE infinitive
steps.a: I find it hard not to fall asleep
steps.why: not goes in front of the to, never between to and the verb.

steps.cue: Now say the lecture itself is dull, using an -ING subject

write.q: Write about 180 words on what actually bores you, and on the difference between the boredom you can escape and the boredom you cannot. Use at least two -ing forms after prepositions, two infinitives after adjectives, one -ing form as the subject of a sentence, and one too or enough pattern.
plan: what bores you most, and why
which one is actually the problem
write.model:
What bores me is not doing nothing. Sitting on a train for six hours with no signal is, if anything, a relief.

What I am fed up with is waiting for other people to decide things. Being in a meeting where the decision was taken before anybody arrived is the closest I get to genuine boredom at work, and it is exhausting in a way that hard work never is.

The boredom you can escape is easy. A dull book is too dull to finish, so you stop; a bad film is not good enough to justify two hours, so you leave.

The other kind is the problem. I find it hard not to look at my phone in a queue, which is not because the queue is unbearable. It is because I have stopped being able to stand ten minutes of nothing, and that is a habit I acquired rather than a fact about me.
